claims.text: At high temperatures, FeNiCrCoCu thin-film wear resistance is governed by formation of an in-situ oxide layer.
The oxide layer is stable and self-healing.
The oxide layer reduces direct metal–metal contact and friction during wear.
A typical FeNiCrCoCu thin film produced by standard processing has a nanocrystalline grain structure.
Controlled high-temperature annealing can intentionally form an oxide scale on the FeNiCrCoCu coating before wear testing.
Temperatures above approximately 500°C provide favorable oxidation kinetics for the proposed protective oxide.
The relevant structural mediator is a fine-grained, adherent surface oxide layer.
Elevated temperature drives selective oxidation of one or more FeNiCrCoCu constituents.
The resulting oxide film acts as a lubricious and protective barrier.
The oxide barrier minimizes plastic deformation and abrasive and adhesive wear by reducing direct engagement between metallic surfaces under high load.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower high-temperature wear rates than as-deposited coatings.
Pre-oxidized FeNiCrCoCu coatings will have lower high-temperature friction coefficients than as-deposited coatings.
Surface analysis of pre-oxidized samples should reveal a continuous, adherent oxide scale.
Substrate oxidation or coating–substrate thermal-expansion mismatch may alter wear performance.
